# Change request procedure — FigDown

This is a `flowchart` (states/decision/outcome with one flow through them, not a node-and-edge graph of arbitrary relationships), so I loaded `reference/experimental/flowchart.md` and `reference/layout.md` per the router. `flowchart` is EXPERIMENTAL (dispatchable at `figdown 0.1`, no version bump), which I'm noting here per the portability rule since I'm choosing it over the "portable three."

The "change window" enclosure is a grouping construct around `validate` and `apply` — this states a scope, not a flow step, so it's expressed as a container around those two node ids rather than as an extra node in the chain.

```figdown
# FigDown — figures as text. Spec: https://github.com/FigDown/figdown
figdown 0.1 flowchart
title "Change request procedure"

process receive "Receive change request"
process validate "Validate against policy"
decision isvalid "Valid?"
process apply "Apply change to device"
terminator confirm "Confirm success"
terminator rollback "Roll back"

group window "Change window" { validate apply }

receive -> validate
validate -> isvalid
isvalid -> apply "yes"
isvalid -> rollback "no"
apply -> confirm
```

![Change request procedure: receive, validate against policy, then branch on validity — apply and confirm on the yes path, roll back on the no path; validate and apply sit inside the change window](figures/change-request-procedure.svg)

<sub>source: [figures/change-request-procedure.fd](figures/change-request-procedure.fd)</sub>

Next step per the workflow: run `node <skill-dir>/build-svg.js change-request-procedure.fd`, fix any `Line N:` errors it reports (in particular, confirm the exact `group` keyword/brace syntax against `reference/experimental/flowchart.md` if the build rejects it), then look at the render to confirm the change-window box visibly encloses just `validate` and `apply`.
